selected_mathematical_checks: The source gives a genuinely uniform C_epsilon over normalized schlicht maps, not only B_S(-2)=1. With q=u/2 and epsilon=(1-q)/(2q), q(1+epsilon)=(1+q)/2<1. Integrating 2pi r dr and using r<=1 gives the stated safe 4pi C_epsilon^q/(1-q) term; the inner disk bound is (pi/4)(27/4)^u.

The subcritical tail is Markov with the actual K_j; area change from D to W multiplies by |h|^-2, so the inverse-map tail is bounded by lambda^-2 times the D-tail. The fourth-power weighted inverse integral equals the square-power integral on D exactly, including an arbitrary positive denominator.

The recursive T_j may be chosen finite for each j without an effective growth law for source constants. The running supremum Lambda is finite on compact intervals and nondecreasing. On late bands g(t)<=t^(2/j); all earlier bands have finite supremum. This proves log Lambda/log t->0. Each high band costs at most 2^-j and the sum for j>=2 is 1/2. No fixed logarithmic power follows.

The positive weighted shift is continuous at the one-point compactification because weights tend to one. Its n-step weights telescope; concavity of sqrt makes j=0 maximal, giving norm exp(sqrt(n)) and spectral radius one. Scaling by two proves only an abstract spectral-radius obstruction, not a conformal counterexample.

For a set of area m, integral_E |z-zeta|^-1 <= integral min(m,pi t^-2)dt =2 sqrt(pi m). Tonelli against total variation gives (lambda-B)m<=2sqrt(pi)M sqrt(m), hence the exact 4pi M²/(lambda-B)² bound. For lambda>=max(2,2B), use C=16pi M².

On the jth dyadic band, t²<=4(L2^j)² and tail mass<=C/(L2^j)²; log(e+t)>=(j+1)log2. Summing (j+1)^-gamma<=1+1/(gamma-1) gives the displayed 64pi M² term. The low band costs <=pi L². Level-set endpoints are null except the normalized constant h=1, already in the low band.

Meromorphic extension across the compact closed disk gives finitely many derivative zeros and poles. Interior injectivity excludes derivative zeros in D. A boundary zero of order >=2 contradicts the radial distortion lower bound proportional to 1-r; every reciprocal pole is simple with residue 1/fdoubleprime(zeta). Subtracting all principal parts leaves a bounded analytic remainder on a neighborhood of the closed disk.

Near a simple boundary pole, high-level sets are sandwiched by radii |c|/(lambda plus/minus A), and the disk intersection is asymptotically a half-disk. This yields pi|c|²/2 for lambda² area on D. Integrating |z-zeta|²/|c|² over the same half-disk yields pi|c|²/4 for the inverse-map lambda^4 tail. These are fixed-map asymptotics without uniform family remainders.

Koebe reciprocal derivative has exact partial fraction -z²+4z-7+8/(1+z); residue 8 gives 32pi and 16pi. Its weighted square integral is equivalent near -1 to integral dr/[r(log(1/r))^gamma], so gamma<=1 fails within S. The safe criterion parameters B=12, M=8 follow directly. It does not decide gamma>1.

Prescribing o(sqrt(N)) signs changes the circle supremum by at most twice the prefix length. A slowly decreasing error sequence is available from all-N source thresholds; this does not build one compatible infinite sign sequence.
